thread:
maria: Heads-up: Azure reseller FinEdge just flagged a settlement discrepancy for March marketplace usage. They say the settlement file withheld VAT on reseller payouts and also shows list-rate instead of committed tier for one SKU.
ashok: VAT? We normally don't withhold VAT on reseller payouts. Can you paste their settlement row + our invoice line?
maria: Partner attached settlement CSV row:
```
sku,units,unit_settled,vat_withheld
redwood_platform_b1,300,1.20,18.00
```
Our invoice line:
```
INV-2026-03-4100
SKU: redwood_platform_b1
Qty: 300
List price: $1.50
Committed discount 20% -> net $1.20
Line net: $360.00
```
maria: Partner claims they received 300 * 1.20 = $360 but Azure withheld VAT of $18 in settlement, so partner received $342. They expected no VAT holdback and asked us to confirm.
billing-bot: settlement export for merchant=finedge on 2026-03-31 completed. Applied pricing profile: PROFILE_COMMITTED_20. No VAT flag set on our side. Export id: AZ-EXP-1799701122.
ashok: So our exporter used committed profile (good). VAT holdback must be on Azure side. Sophie, did partner provide Azure support ticket?
sophie: Yes they opened ticket AZ-99211. Azure says VAT retained per local tax rule because reseller submitted EU VAT registration but settlement opted to withhold for that payout window. They suggest partner dispute with Azure tax team.
maria: Partner wants us to issue a credit for the $18 VAT retention so they net to expected. Do we approve marketplace tax indemnity credits?
kelly: AP here. Policy: we only credit taxes when Redwood is legally responsible or if the platform incorrectly applied our tax settings. We need proof Azure misapplied our VAT configuration or confirmation that Redwood is liable.
ashok: billing-bot, does our merchant profile for finedge have tax_responsibility = "partner" or "redwood"?
billing-bot: merchant_profile for finedge: tax_responsibility=partner; vat_id=EU-12345X.
maria: So partner declared VAT responsibility. Looks like Azure withheld anyway. Kelly, we likely shouldn't absorb VAT unless legal advises. But to keep partner calm, we can offer a provisional marketplace adjustment of $18 with a reimbursement clause if Azure reverses it. Need AP ok.
kelly: I can approve provisional adjustment only if legal signs off on the reimbursement clause and we tag it as provisional. Also need reconciliation export and Azure ticket.
sophie: Attached: s3://redwood-billing/azure/recons/2026-03/finedge-vat-1799701122.csv and ticket AZ-99211. I'll loop in legal.
maria: Also note partner flagged a separate line: an old SKU alias redwood_platform_b1_legacy was billed at list $1.50 for 50 units, but their partner margin calc expected committed $1.20. billing-bot said committed profile applied, but partner shows 50 units at 1.50 in settlement.
billing-bot: cross-check: 50 units for SKU alias redwood_platform_b1_legacy mapped to PROFILE_PUBLIC_LEGACY in Azure feed on 2026-03-31.
ashok: That's the mapping bug again. Action items: 1) Sophie to get Azure to reprocess or provide VAT refund confirmation 2) Finance/AP to approve provisional $18 adjustment with legal clause 3) Engineering to fix alias->profile mapping for Azure feed and add a test to prevent legacy fallback. James, can you own engineering?
sophie: I'll keep partner updated and post ticket links.
maria: Kelly, please prepare provisional credit memo CM-2026-03-010 for $18 to FinEdge pending legal review and final Azure outcome. Include invoice INV-2026-03-4100 and AZ-99211.
kelly: Will prepare provisional CM and route for e-sign. Posting ETA 2 business days.
maria: Thanks. Leaving thread open until CM posted and Azure confirms tax holdback outcome. :slightly_smiling_face:
